Data management tools

Source: vignettes/data-management.Rmd
data-management.Rmd

This vignette covers the helpers for setting up a study, importing and checking data, and recoding and summarising variables. They follow the steps of the pipeline described in vignette("data_analysis_pipeline", package = "C306").

Step Functions
Set up a project createProject()
Import a data dictionary import.info(), convert.info()
Format and check data myformat.data(), inspect.data(), getlabel()
Recode and reorder simple_recode(), simple_relevel(), simple_sort(), ref_lv()
Derive and summarise mutate_f(), summarise_f(), labAE(), contSummary(), pct() 
library(C306)

The examples use baseline_data and ae_data, a simulated two-arm trial bundled with the package.

Set up a project: createProject()

createProject() copies a standard folder structure, with template scripts for importing, cleaning, analysing and reporting, into a new folder and adds an RStudio project file. It refuses to write into a folder that is not empty.

proj <- file.path(tempdir(), "myStudy")
createProject(proj)
#> Project myStudy was created in /tmp/RtmpaRP1hy
list.files(proj, recursive = TRUE)
#>  [1] "Analysis/01_import.R"                                                
#>  [2] "Analysis/02_clean.R"                                                 
#>  [3] "Analysis/03_createVAD.R"

Import a data dictionary

import.info()

OUCRU data dictionaries are Excel files with a CRFs sheet, a Grids sheet and one sheet per CRF. import.info() reads the requested sheets and saves one data frame per sheet, <sheet>_info, in an .RData file. A grid is requested as <CRF>_<Grid>. The package includes a small example dictionary:

dict <- system.file("extdata", "oucru_dictionary.xlsx", package = "C306")
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".RData")
import.info(c("ENR", "LAB", "LAB_G1"), input = dict, output = out)
load(out)
sheet_info_name
#> [1] "ENR_info"    "LAB_info"    "LAB_G1_info"
ENR_info
#> # A tibble: 3 × 8
#>   Variable Caption        `Data type` Category Format   Grid  Note1 Note2
#>   <chr>    <chr>          <chr>       <chr>    <chr>    <lgl> <lgl> <lgl>
#> 1 AGE      Age            Integer     NA       NA       NA    NA    NA   
#> 2 SEX      Sex            RadioList   SEX      NA       NA    NA    NA   
#> 3 ENRDATE  Enrolment date DateTime    NA       dd/mm/yy NA    NA    NA

convert.info()

convert.info() turns an OUCRU dictionary and its category list into the general dictionary format used by myformat.data() and inspect.data(), with columns varname, label, type, unit, value, levels and missing:

oucru_info <- data.frame(
  Category = c(NA, "SEX"), Variable = c("AGE", "SEX"), Caption = c("Age", "Sex"),
  `Data type` = c("Integer", "RadioList"), Format = NA, check.names = FALSE
)
oucru_category <- data.frame(category = "SEX", submissionvalue = c("1", "2"),
                             text = c("Male", "Female"))
convert.info(oucru_info, oucru_category)
#>   varname label    type unit               value          levels missing scale
#> 1     SEX   Sex  factor   NA 1='Male';2='Female' 'Male';'Female'      NA    NA
#> 2     AGE   Age numeric   NA                <NA>            <NA>      NA    NA
#>   condition strict
#> 1        NA    Yes
#> 2        NA    Yes

Format and check data

myformat.data()

myformat.data() applies a dictionary to raw data: it converts types, turns codes into labelled factor levels, parses dates, sets missing-value codes to NA and stores labels and units as attributes. Each row of the dictionary describes one variable:

  • type: numeric, factor, character or datetime
  • value: the code-to-label map of a factor (1='Male';2='Female'), the date format of a datetime (ymd), or the allowed range of a number (0;100, used by inspect.data())
  • levels: the order of the factor levels
  • missing: codes that mean missing, e.g. -99

Here we take a few columns of the simulated trial and introduce two errors: an age of 150 and an ASA status of 4.

raw <- head(baseline_data[, c("usubjid", "age", "asa", "timetoadm")], 8)
raw$age[3] <- 150
raw$asa[5] <- 4
raw$timetoadm[6] <- -99

info <- data.frame(
  varname = c("usubjid", "age", "asa", "timetoadm"),
  label = c("Participant ID", "Age", "ASA physical status", "Time to admission"),
  type = c("character", "numeric", "factor", "numeric"),
  unit = c(NA, "years", NA, "days"),
  value = c(NA, "0;100", "1='ASA I';2='ASA II';3='ASA III'", "0;60"),
  levels = c(NA, NA, "'ASA I';'ASA II';'ASA III'", NA),
  missing = c(NA, NA, NA, "-99")
)

dat <- myformat.data(raw, info)
#> Warning: asa: value(s) not in the dictionary kept as extra level(s): 4.
str(dat)
#> 'data.frame':    8 obs. of  4 variables:
#>  $ usubjid  : chr  "SIM-001" "SIM-002" "SIM-003" "SIM-004" ...
#>  $ age      : num  63 43 150 18 53 51 77 37
#>   ..- attr(*, "label")= chr "Age"
#>   ..- attr(*, "unit")= chr "years"
#>   ..- attr(*, "scale")= num 1
#>   ..- attr(*, "center")= num 0
#>  $ asa      : Factor w/ 4 levels "ASA I","ASA II",..: 2 1 2 2 4 2 1 1
#>   ..- attr(*, "label")= chr "ASA physical status"
#>  $ timetoadm: num  11 3 5 4 21 NA 2 4
#>   ..- attr(*, "label")= chr "Time to admission"
#>   ..- attr(*, "unit")= chr "days"
#>   ..- attr(*, "scale")= num 1
#>   ..- attr(*, "center")= num 0

The warning flags the ASA code that is not in the dictionary; it is kept as an extra level so that it can be reported.

inspect.data()

inspect.data() checks formatted data against the dictionary and lists values out of range, codes not in the dictionary and missing values. The list is returned and also written to <prefix>_error.csv in outdir (plot = TRUE also saves the distribution of each variable to a PDF).

inspect.data(dat, info, id = "usubjid", outdir = tempdir())
#>          usubjid index                       error
#> 1 "=""SIM-003"""     3     Out of range: age > 100
#> 2 "=""SIM-005"""     5       Out of range: asa = 4
#> 3 "=""SIM-006"""     6 Missing value for timetoadm

getlabel()

getlabel() returns the label of a variable, with its unit, from its attributes or from a dictionary. With fit = TRUE it describes the variable as it enters a model, using the scale attribute (e.g. “per 10 years”):

wt <- structure(c(60, 72), label = "Weight", unit = "kg", scale = 10)
getlabel(wt)
#> [1] "Weight [kg]"
getlabel(wt, fit = TRUE)
#> [1] "Weight [+10 kg]"

meta <- data.frame(varname = c("age", "sex"), label = c("Age", "Sex"),
                   unit = c("years", NA), scale = c(10, NA),
                   type = c("numeric", "factor"))
getlabel("age", meta = meta)
#> [1] "Age [years]"
getlabel(baseline_data[, c("age", "sex")], meta = meta)
#> [1] "Age [years]" "Sex"

Recode and reorder

simple_recode()

simple_recode() recodes values that match regular expressions; values that match no pattern are kept. A pattern of NA recodes missing values.

simple_recode(c("yes", "Yes", "no", NA),
              map = list(Y = "^[Yy]es$", N = "^no$", Unknown = NA))
#> [1] "Y"       "Y"       "N"       "Unknown"

A factor stays a factor, and as converts the result. For a data frame, give one map per variable:

recoded <- simple_recode(head(baseline_data[, c("sex", "vaso")]),
                         sex = list(Female = "^F$", Male = "^M$"),
                         vaso = list(Yes = "^Y$", No = "^N$"))
recoded
#>      sex vaso
#> 1 Female   No
#> 2   Male   No
#> 3   Male   No
#> 4 Female   No
#> 5   Male   No
#> 6 Female   No

simple_relevel()

simple_relevel() orders the levels of one variable to follow another factor. For example, to list AE terms grouped by organ class in the order of the classes:

grp <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "group_data.csv", package = "C306"))
grp$class <- factor(grp$class)
grp2 <- simple_relevel(grp, ctcaename, by = class)
head(levels(grp2$ctcaename))
#> [1] "Allergy"                  "Pruritus"                
#> [3] "Skin allergy"             "Arterial thromboembolism"
#> [5] "Atrial fibrillation"      "Atrial thrombosis"

For a vector, give the grouping factor and a map from each group to its values:

simple_relevel(c("p", "q", "r"), by = factor(c("B", "A", "B"), levels = c("B", "A")),
               map = list(A = "q", B = c("p", "r")), value = "levels")
#> [1] "p" "r" "q"

simple_sort()

simple_sort() sorts a vector in a user-defined order:

simple_sort(c("III", "I", "II", "I"), order = c("I", "II", "III"))
#> [1] "I"   "I"   "II"  "III"

ref_lv()

ref_lv() gets the reference (first) level of a factor, and ref_lv<- sets it while keeping the order of the other levels:

arm <- factor(baseline_data$Arm)
ref_lv(arm)
#> [1] "Intrathecal treatment"
ref_lv(arm) <- "Sham procedure"
levels(arm)
#> [1] "Sham procedure"        "Intrathecal treatment"

Derive and summarise

mutate_f() and summarise_f()

These work like dplyr::mutate() and dplyr::summarise() but can create several columns in one expression, with c(...) := list(...) in mutate_f() and a named list in summarise_f(). They work on data frames, grouped tibbles and data.tables.

small <- head(baseline_data[, c("usubjid", "Arm", "maxhr", "minhr")], 6)
small %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Arm) %>%
  mutate_f(c("hr_range", "hr_mid") := list(maxhr - minhr, (maxhr + minhr) / 2))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 6
#> # Groups:   Arm [2]
#>   usubjid Arm                   maxhr minhr hr_range hr_mid
#>   <chr>   <chr>                 <int> <int>    <int>  <dbl>
#> 1 SIM-001 Intrathecal treatment   133    92       41  112. 
#> 2 SIM-002 Intrathecal treatment   135    64       71   99.5
#> 3 SIM-003 Sham procedure           84    84        0   84  
#> 4 SIM-004 Intrathecal treatment   106    84       22   95  
#> 5 SIM-005 Sham procedure           95    63       32   79  
#> 6 SIM-006 Sham procedure           82    79        3   80.5

baseline_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Arm) %>%
  summarise_f(list(n = length(age), mean_age = mean(age), max_sofa = max(sofa, na.rm = TRUE)))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#> # Groups:   Arm [2]
#>   Arm                       n mean_age max_sofa
#>   <chr>                 <int>    <dbl>    <int>
#> 1 Intrathecal treatment   136     48.6        7
#> 2 Sham procedure          135     48.7        5

labAE()

For laboratory adverse events graded at each visit, labAE() flags the visits where a new event should be reported: the grade reaches gradecut and is higher than the worst grade so far.

labAE(c(0, 1, 3, 3, 2, 4), gradecut = 3)
#> [1] No  No  Yes No  No  Yes
#> Levels: Yes No

visits <- data.frame(id = rep(c("SIM-001", "SIM-002"), each = 3),
                     grade = c(1, 3, 3, 3, 2, 4))
visits %>%
  dplyr::group_by(id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(new_ae = labAE(grade, gradecut = 3))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#> # Groups:   id [2]
#>   id      grade new_ae
#>   <chr>   <dbl> <fct> 
#> 1 SIM-001     1 No    
#> 2 SIM-001     3 Yes   
#> 3 SIM-001     3 No    
#> 4 SIM-002     3 Yes   
#> 5 SIM-002     2 No    
#> 6 SIM-002     4 Yes

contSummary()

contSummary() formats summary statistics of a numeric vector as text. The statistics string is a template: the words mean, sd, median, Q1, Q3, min and max (in any case) are replaced by their values and all other text is kept. This is what sstable.baseline() uses for continuous variables.

contSummary(baseline_data$bmi, "mean (sd)")
#> [1] "21.3 (3.7)"
contSummary(baseline_data$age, "median (Q1-Q3)", digits = 0)
#> [1] "49 (38-59)"
contSummary(baseline_data$icudays, "Median [IQR: Q1-Q3], range min-max", digits = 0)
#> [1] "17 [IQR: 11-23], range 3-58"

pct()

pct() returns proportions: the percentage of TRUE for a logical vector, one per level for a factor, or one per interval for a number cut at breaks.

pct(baseline_data$vaso == "Y")
#> [1] 12.54613
pct(factor(baseline_data$ablettscore))
#>        I       II      III 
#> 38.00738 42.43542 19.55720
pct(baseline_data$age, method = "cont", breaks = c(0, 40, 60, 100))
#>   (0,40]  (40,60] (60,100] 
#> 30.99631 47.23247 21.77122
